samples.scenario: Prediction target period: from 2023-10-29 to 2024-01-14. Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> The US-registered WorldTour cycling team, Lidl-Trek, announced it has finalized its new 14-rider development team for the 2024 season, a move designed to cultivate talent for its primary WorldTour squad. [1, 2] This strategy aligns Lidl-Trek with other top-level teams, such as Groupama-FDJ and EF Education-EasyPost, that run their own continental development programs. [1] The team's inaugural roster includes American rider Cole Kessler, who is the only U.S. racer in the squad. [2] The complete 14-rider team for 2024 consists of: Nils Aebersold (Switzerland), Niklas Behrens (Germany), Kristian Egholm (Denmark), Patrick Boje Frydkjær (Denmark), Cole Kessler (USA), Louis Leidert (Germany), Matteo Milan (Italy), Liam O’Brien (Ireland), Martin Pedersen (Denmark), Cameron Rogers (Australia), Jakob Soderqvist (Sweden), Tim Torn Teutenberg (Germany), Axandre van Petegem (Belgium), and Mats Wenzel (Luxembourg). [2] <2> In an interview from the Tour of Guangxi, American cyclist Matteo Jorgenson elaborated on his decision to sign with Jumbo-Visma, stating his primary motivation was to reach his highest physical potential. He acknowledged the challenge of securing a spot on the team for the Tour de France, recognizing it is not guaranteed. Jorgenson expressed his ambition to earn his place, stating, "On a team like Jumbo-Visma you have to earn your spot... It’s always the eight best guys that go to the Tour. I’ll try my best to be there for sure." He further explained his long-term perspective on the move: "I really wanted to find a place where I could become the best version of myself... At this point in my career while I’m still young and still have a margin for progression, I want to go to a place where I can get the most out of myself physically and reach my best level." <3> To honor his victory at the 2023 Vuelta a España, American cyclist Sepp Kuss was celebrated with a homecoming event in his native Durango, Colorado. [7] The win made Kuss the first American in a decade to win a Grand Tour. [7] Hosted by Durango Devo, the youth cycling program Kuss is an alumnus of, the celebration took place on October 19, 2023, at Buckley Park. [2, 7] The event was part of 'Spoketober,' a month-long celebration of cycling in the town. [4, 8] The festivities drew an estimated 2,225 people and included speeches from Kuss and Durango Mayor Melissa Youssef, a Q&A session, and a public bike parade down Main Avenue. [3, 7, 9] The celebration concluded with live music, food, and an autograph session where Kuss signed memorabilia for nearly two hours, far longer than originally planned due to the massive turnout. [7] <4> A viewership analysis of the 2023 Tour de France in the United States revealed a marginal overall increase in streaming viewership over the 23-day race. [3] However, the final stage into Paris on July 23, 2023, experienced a significant surge, with a 78% increase in plays, a 46% rise in unique viewers, and a 40% growth in total playtime as Danish cyclist Jonas Vingegaard secured his second consecutive victory. [3, 6] Despite the final day's success, data suggests that live streaming for cycling does not have the same broad appeal as other live sports, with the Tour appealing to a more specific audience. [3] The primary viewing devices for the event were pay-TV set-top boxes and large-screen televisions, accounting for 75% of the total playtime. [3] <5> A report published on July 25, 2023, detailed the performance of the six American riders who participated in the 2023 Tour de France, which concluded on July 23, 2023. [2] Out of the six American starters, four completed the race and arrived in Paris. [2] The analysis highlighted the achievements of Sepp Kuss (Jumbo-Visma), who finished 12th in the overall classification. [2] It also focused on Neilson Powless (EF Education-EasyPost), who distinguished himself by winning the King of the Mountains jersey on the opening stage and holding it for all but one day until well into the third week of the competition. [2] <6> Six American cyclists were confirmed on their respective teams' rosters for the 2023 Tour de France, which began on July 1, 2023, in Bilbao, Spain. The riders included Sepp Kuss for Jumbo-Visma, Neilson Powless for EF Education-EasyPost, Quinn Simmons for Lidl-Trek, Lawson Craddock for Team Jayco AlUla, Matteo Jorgenson for Movistar, and Kevin Vermaerke for Team dsm-firmenich. Roster announcements were made in the days leading up to the event, with several teams confirming their lineups by June 26, 2023. Kuss was a key support rider for the overall winner, Jonas Vingegaard. Powless notably held the King of the Mountains jersey for thirteen stages. Simmons, the reigning US national champion, was forced to abandon the race after a crash. <7> Quinn Simmons of Trek-Segafredo secured a solo victory in the men's elite road race at the USA Cycling Pro Road National Championships in Knoxville, Tennessee on June 25, 2023. This was his first national title in the elite category, earning him the right to wear the stars and stripes jersey in competition. Following the win, Simmons participated in the 2023 Tour de France, but his race was cut short when he abandoned ahead of stage 9 due to injuries sustained in a crash. <8> On June 15, 2023, NBC Sports officially announced its comprehensive broadcast schedule for the 110th Tour de France. [6] The coverage featured live, start-to-finish streaming of all 21 stages on Peacock. [6, 8] In addition to the Peacock stream, select stages were broadcast on NBC and USA Network. [6, 8] The 110th edition of the Tour de France took place from July 1, 2023, to July 23, 2023, starting in Bilbao, Spain, and concluding at the Champs-Élysées in Paris. [2, 3, 4, 7] <9> Three-time Tour de France winner Greg LeMond participated in the 18th annual 'Face of America: Gettysburg,' an adaptive cycling challenge that honors the sacrifices and dedication of America's adaptive military veterans. The non-competitive event, which involved roughly 400 cyclists including 75 adaptive riders, ran from April 21-23, 2023. Participants cycled a 110-mile route from Arlington (Crystal City), Virginia, to the historic community of Gettysburg, Pennsylvania. <10> Netflix announced its eight-part documentary series covering the 2022 Tour de France would be titled 'Tour de France: Unchained'. Produced by Quadbox and Box to Box Films, the makers of 'Formula 1: Drive to Survive', the series was created to make the sport more accessible and attract a wider international audience. While an early trailer was screened in February 2023, the official public trailer, title, and release date were promoted in April 2023. The series, which follows several cycling teams through the celebrated and grueling race, was released on the streaming platform on June 8, 2023.

This marks a significant expansion for ENVE, which for the first time will supply a WorldTour team with its Melee road bike frames in addition to its full range of SES wheels, tires, and cockpit components. The partnership, which includes a research and development collaboration, will see the team compete in major events, including the Tour de France, on ENVE equipment. This deal replaces Specialized as the team's previous equipment sponsor and runs alongside ENVE's existing agreements to supply wheels and components to UAE Team Emirates and Team Polti Kometa. <2> The route for the third edition of the Tour de France Femmes was officially unveiled in Paris on October 25, 2023. Due to the 2024 Olympic Games in Paris, the race was rescheduled to mid-August. <3> The US-registered WorldTour cycling team, Lidl-Trek, announced it has finalized its new 14-rider development team for the 2024 season, a move designed to cultivate talent for its primary WorldTour squad. [1, 2] This strategy aligns Lidl-Trek with other top-level teams, such as Groupama-FDJ and EF Education-EasyPost, that run their own continental development programs. [1] The team's inaugural roster includes American rider Cole Kessler, who is the only U.S. racer in the squad. [2] The complete 14-rider team for 2024 consists of: Nils Aebersold (Switzerland), Niklas Behrens (Germany), Kristian Egholm (Denmark), Patrick Boje Frydkjær (Denmark), Cole Kessler (USA), Louis Leidert (Germany), Matteo Milan (Italy), Liam O’Brien (Ireland), Martin Pedersen (Denmark), Cameron Rogers (Australia), Jakob Soderqvist (Sweden), Tim Torn Teutenberg (Germany), Axandre van Petegem (Belgium), and Mats Wenzel (Luxembourg). [2] <4> In an interview from the Tour of Guangxi, American cyclist Matteo Jorgenson elaborated on his decision to sign with Jumbo-Visma, stating his primary motivation was to reach his highest physical potential. He acknowledged the challenge of securing a spot on the team for the Tour de France, recognizing it is not guaranteed. Jorgenson expressed his ambition to earn his place, stating, "On a team like Jumbo-Visma you have to earn your spot... It’s always the eight best guys that go to the Tour. I’ll try my best to be there for sure." He further explained his long-term perspective on the move: "I really wanted to find a place where I could become the best version of myself... At this point in my career while I’m still young and still have a margin for progression, I want to go to a place where I can get the most out of myself physically and reach my best level." <5> To honor his victory at the 2023 Vuelta a España, American cyclist Sepp Kuss was celebrated with a homecoming event in his native Durango, Colorado. [7] The win made Kuss the first American in a decade to win a Grand Tour. [7] Hosted by Durango Devo, the youth cycling program Kuss is an alumnus of, the celebration took place on October 19, 2023, at Buckley Park. [2, 7] The event was part of 'Spoketober,' a month-long celebration of cycling in the town. [4, 8] The festivities drew an estimated 2,225 people and included speeches from Kuss and Durango Mayor Melissa Youssef, a Q&A session, and a public bike parade down Main Avenue. [3, 7, 9] The celebration concluded with live music, food, and an autograph session where Kuss signed memorabilia for nearly two hours, far longer than originally planned due to the massive turnout. [7] <6> A viewership analysis of the 2023 Tour de France in the United States revealed a marginal overall increase in streaming viewership over the 23-day race. [3] However, the final stage into Paris on July 23, 2023, experienced a significant surge, with a 78% increase in plays, a 46% rise in unique viewers, and a 40% growth in total playtime as Danish cyclist Jonas Vingegaard secured his second consecutive victory. [3, 6] Despite the final day's success, data suggests that live streaming for cycling does not have the same broad appeal as other live sports, with the Tour appealing to a more specific audience. [3] The primary viewing devices for the event were pay-TV set-top boxes and large-screen televisions, accounting for 75% of the total playtime. [3] <7> A report published on July 25, 2023, detailed the performance of the six American riders who participated in the 2023 Tour de France, which concluded on July 23, 2023. [2] Out of the six American starters, four completed the race and arrived in Paris. [2] The analysis highlighted the achievements of Sepp Kuss (Jumbo-Visma), who finished 12th in the overall classification. [2] It also focused on Neilson Powless (EF Education-EasyPost), who distinguished himself by winning the King of the Mountains jersey on the opening stage and holding it for all but one day until well into the third week of the competition. [2] <8> Six American cyclists were confirmed on their respective teams' rosters for the 2023 Tour de France, which began on July 1, 2023, in Bilbao, Spain. The riders included Sepp Kuss for Jumbo-Visma, Neilson Powless for EF Education-EasyPost, Quinn Simmons for Lidl-Trek, Lawson Craddock for Team Jayco AlUla, Matteo Jorgenson for Movistar, and Kevin Vermaerke for Team dsm-firmenich. Roster announcements were made in the days leading up to the event, with several teams confirming their lineups by June 26, 2023. Kuss was a key support rider for the overall winner, Jonas Vingegaard. Powless notably held the King of the Mountains jersey for thirteen stages. Simmons, the reigning US national champion, was forced to abandon the race after a crash. <9> Quinn Simmons of Trek-Segafredo secured a solo victory in the men's elite road race at the USA Cycling Pro Road National Championships in Knoxville, Tennessee on June 25, 2023. This was his first national title in the elite category, earning him the right to wear the stars and stripes jersey in competition. Following the win, Simmons participated in the 2023 Tour de France, but his race was cut short when he abandoned ahead of stage 9 due to injuries sustained in a crash. <10> On June 15, 2023, NBC Sports officially announced its comprehensive broadcast schedule for the 110th Tour de France. [6] The coverage featured live, start-to-finish streaming of all 21 stages on Peacock. [6, 8] In addition to the Peacock stream, select stages were broadcast on NBC and USA Network. [6, 8] The 110th edition of the Tour de France took place from July 1, 2023, to July 23, 2023, starting in Bilbao, Spain, and concluding at the Champs-Élysées in Paris. [2, 3, 4, 7]

[2]

metadata.original_text: This time series records tour de france data in the web search domain, with a collection frequency of weekly, focusing on monitoring and analyzing relevant indicators. Prediction target period: from 2024-10-27 to 2025-01-12. Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> Media outlets reported on the participation of American cyclists Matteo Jorgenson (Visma-Lease a Bike), Neilson Powless (EF Education-EasyPost), and Sean Quinn (EF Education-EasyPost) in the 2024 Tour de France, which ran from June 29 to July 21, 2024. [2, 3] Pre-race analysis highlighted Jorgenson, in his third Tour, as a key support rider for Jonas Vingegaard and a potential contender himself, following his victory at Paris-Nice earlier in the year. [8, 18] Powless, starting his fifth Tour, aimed for a stage victory after a season hampered by a knee injury. [8, 11, 18] Making his debut, U.S. champion Sean Quinn was expected to support his team leaders. [8, 15] During the race, Jorgenson achieved a significant milestone, finishing eighth in the general classification, the first top-10 finish for an American rider since 2014. [17] He also came agonizingly close to a victory on Stage 19. [7] Powless and Quinn were both involved in a crash during Stage 12; Powless sustained a minor wrist fracture but both were able to continue. [6] Powless was a key contributor to his teammate Richard Carapaz's victory in the King of the Mountains classification. [14] <2> It was announced on June 21, 2024, that Tao Geoghegan Hart will miss the 2024 Tour de France. The 2020 Giro d'Italia winner was scheduled to lead his American-licensed team, Lidl-Trek, but has been sidelined due to a fractured rib sustained in a crash at the Critérium du Dauphiné and a subsequent COVID-19 infection. This would have been the first time Geoghegan Hart was to have a leadership role at the Tour de France. <3> The 2024 L'Étape Las Vegas by Tour de France, an amateur cycling event with 75-mile, 45-mile, and 25-mile course options through the Red Rock Canyon National Conservation Area, was scheduled to occur on May 5, 2024. The initial announcement for the event's return was made on March 7, 2024. However, on May 4, 2024, organizers announced the cancellation of the event due to a forecast of high winds that were deemed unsafe for participants, staff, and vendors. Riders who had registered for the 2024 event, representing 30 states and 8 countries, were automatically deferred to the 2025 event. <4> American cyclist Joe Dombrowski announced his retirement from professional cycling on January 23, 2024, after a 12-year career. [3, 5] The decision came after his contract with the Astana Qazaqstan Team was not renewed for the 2024 season and a subsequent search for a new team was unsuccessful. [2, 3] A veteran of 14 Grand Tours, Dombrowski's career highlights include a stage victory at the 2021 Giro d'Italia. [3, 6] He turned professional in 2013 with Team Sky and also rode for teams including Cannondale/EF Education First and UAE Team Emirates before his final two seasons with Astana Qazaqstan. [2, 3] <5> Utah-based sporting goods company ENVE announced it would serve as a primary equipment sponsor for the French professional cycling team, Team TotalEnergies, for the 2024 and 2025 seasons. This marks a significant expansion for ENVE, which for the first time will supply a WorldTour team with its Melee road bike frames in addition to its full range of SES wheels, tires, and cockpit components. The partnership, which includes a research and development collaboration, will see the team compete in major events, including the Tour de France, on ENVE equipment. This deal replaces Specialized as the team's previous equipment sponsor and runs alongside ENVE's existing agreements to supply wheels and components to UAE Team Emirates and Team Polti Kometa. <6> The route for the third edition of the Tour de France Femmes was officially unveiled in Paris on October 25, 2023. Due to the 2024 Olympic Games in Paris, the race was rescheduled to mid-August. The event took place from August 12 to August 18, 2024. The 946.3km race began with a Grand Départ in the Netherlands, the first time the event started outside of France. The route featured eight stages over seven days, traversing through Belgium before entering France. It concluded with a demanding summit finish on the iconic Alpe d'Huez. Kasia Niewiadoma was crowned the overall winner. <7> The US-registered WorldTour cycling team, Lidl-Trek, announced it has finalized its new 14-rider development team for the 2024 season, a move designed to cultivate talent for its primary WorldTour squad. [1, 2] This strategy aligns Lidl-Trek with other top-level teams, such as Groupama-FDJ and EF Education-EasyPost, that run their own continental development programs. [1] The team's inaugural roster includes American rider Cole Kessler, who is the only U.S. racer in the squad. [2] The complete 14-rider team for 2024 consists of: Nils Aebersold (Switzerland), Niklas Behrens (Germany), Kristian Egholm (Denmark), Patrick Boje Frydkjær (Denmark), Cole Kessler (USA), Louis Leidert (Germany), Matteo Milan (Italy), Liam O’Brien (Ireland), Martin Pedersen (Denmark), Cameron Rogers (Australia), Jakob Soderqvist (Sweden), Tim Torn Teutenberg (Germany), Axandre van Petegem (Belgium), and Mats Wenzel (Luxembourg). [2] <8> In an interview from the Tour of Guangxi, American cyclist Matteo Jorgenson elaborated on his decision to sign with Jumbo-Visma, stating his primary motivation was to reach his highest physical potential. He acknowledged the challenge of securing a spot on the team for the Tour de France, recognizing it is not guaranteed. Jorgenson expressed his ambition to earn his place, stating, "On a team like Jumbo-Visma you have to earn your spot... It’s always the eight best guys that go to the Tour. I’ll try my best to be there for sure." He further explained his long-term perspective on the move: "I really wanted to find a place where I could become the best version of myself... At this point in my career while I’m still young and still have a margin for progression, I want to go to a place where I can get the most out of myself physically and reach my best level." <9> To honor his victory at the 2023 Vuelta a España, American cyclist Sepp Kuss was celebrated with a homecoming event in his native Durango, Colorado. [7] The win made Kuss the first American in a decade to win a Grand Tour. [7] Hosted by Durango Devo, the youth cycling program Kuss is an alumnus of, the celebration took place on October 19, 2023, at Buckley Park. [2, 7] The event was part of 'Spoketober,' a month-long celebration of cycling in the town. [4, 8] The festivities drew an estimated 2,225 people and included speeches from Kuss and Durango Mayor Melissa Youssef, a Q&A session, and a public bike parade down Main Avenue. [3, 7, 9] The celebration concluded with live music, food, and an autograph session where Kuss signed memorabilia for nearly two hours, far longer than originally planned due to the massive turnout. [7] <10> The US-based professional cycling organization, Human Powered Health, confirmed that its men's UCI ProTeam would cease operations following the 2023 season. [1, 7] The closure was prompted by a lack of sponsorship for the long-running men's program. [7] Initial reports of the team's closure surfaced around August 8, 2023, with management having formally notified riders and staff on August 7, 2023. [3, 4] In the wake of the men's team folding, the organization announced it would pivot to focus exclusively on its Women's WorldTour team for the 2024 season and beyond. [5, 7] This strategic shift included significant investment in the women's squad's structure and roster, which was finalized on November 10, 2023. [2] More than half the team for 2024 consisted of new riders, and the team bolstered its staff by hiring two-time former road world champion Giorgia Bronzini as a directeur sportif, joining a leadership team that includes General Manager Ro de Jonckere and Performance Manager Kenny Latomme. [2]

[2, 3] Pre-race analysis highlighted Jorgenson, in his third Tour, as a key support rider for Jonas Vingegaard and a potential contender himself, following his victory at Paris-Nice earlier in the year. [8, 18] Powless, starting his fifth Tour, aimed for a stage victory after a season hampered by a knee injury. [8, 11, 18] Making his debut, U.S. champion Sean Quinn was expected to support his team leaders. [8, 15] During the race, Jorgenson achieved a significant milestone, finishing eighth in the general classification, the first top-10 finish for an American rider since 2014. [17] He also came agonizingly close to a victory on Stage 19. [7] Powless and Quinn were both involved in a crash during Stage 12; Powless sustained a minor wrist fracture but both were able to continue. [6] Powless was a key contributor to his teammate Richard Carapaz's victory in the King of the Mountains classification. The initial announcement for the event's return was made on March 7, 2024. However, on May 4, 2024, organizers announced the cancellation of the event due to a forecast of high winds that were deemed unsafe for participants, staff, and vendors. Riders who had registered for the 2024 event, representing 30 states and 8 countries, were automatically deferred to the 2025 event.

Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> A comprehensive report was published detailing the 14 American cyclists confirmed to race in the 2026 World Tour peloton, highlighting the roster of riders from the United States for the upcoming professional cycling season. <2> USA Cycling announced the roster of 23 athletes; set to compete in the 2025 UCI Road World Championships in Kigali, Rwanda.; The team announcement specifically mentioned Quinn Simmons, <3> In a New York Times interview published on or around July 20, 2025, Tour de France route designer Thierry Gouvenou stated that a future finish for the race on the U.S. East Coast is a realistic possibility. [4] He expressed a personal preference for this idea over a Grand Départ in the United States, citing the significant time difference and suggesting it would be better for the riders to travel to the U.S. at the conclusion of the race rather than starting there and returning to Europe. [4] This potential shift comes as the race organizers consider new locations for the Tour's finale. [4] <4> The 'Roll with Bob Roll' cycling event took place in Moab, Utah, and was hosted by Bob Roll, a confirmed Tour de France veteran and NBC sports commentator. <5> Bike Works in Newtown, PA, in collaboration with Giant Bicycles, is hosting a watch party for Stage 9 of the 2025 Tour de France on Sunday, July 13, 2025. [4, 5, 13] Although the event was advertised as a viewing for Stage 13, the date corresponds to Stage 9 of the official race schedule. [4, 5] The event, taking place at the Newtown store from 10 AM to Noon, will be preceded by a brisk group ride with Watts & Whiskey Cycling at 8 AM. [4, 11] Participants at the watch party will be entered into a raffle for giveaways, including a Giant TCR Advanced bicycle. [4, 13] <6> On or around July 3, 2025, publications including Cycling Weekly and Velo released analyses and predictions for the North American riders competing in the 2025 Tour de France. [7, 8] The articles focused on a small but strong contingent of five American riders: Sepp Kuss (Visma-Lease a Bike), Matteo Jorgensen (Visma-Lease a Bike), Neilson Powless (EF Education-EasyPost), Quinn Simmons (Lidl-Trek), and Will Barta (Movistar). [7] Simmons entered the Tour as the U.S. national road racing champion. [7] The reports highlighted that the focus for the North American group, which also included two Canadians, was likely to be on securing stage wins. [8] The 112th edition of the Tour de France is scheduled to take place from July 5 to July 27, 2025, beginning in Lille. [2, 3, 4, 5] <7> As part of its July 2025 programming in the United States, TV5MONDE will broadcast the documentary 'Le Tour de France : une passion française' on July 9, 2025, at 8:30pm ET/5:30pm PT. The film examines the 120-year history of the iconic cycling race, which was first held in 1903. Using personal accounts and archival footage, the documentary explores how the Tour de France has become a unifying sporting event and an intrinsic part of France's collective memory and cultural identity. <8> A Redfin article titled 'Is Las Vegas a Good Place to Live? 16 Pros and Cons to Help You Decide,' published on March 19, 2025, features the L'Etape Las Vegas by Tour de France cycling event. The mention was confirmed by a blog post on the official L'Etape Las Vegas website, which celebrated being featured in the Redfin article. The article itself discusses the various benefits and drawbacks of living in the city, using the cycling event as an example of the local culture and activities available to residents. <9> L'Étape Las Vegas by Tour de France, an amateur cycling event that allows participants to experience the legend of the Tour de France, was scheduled to take place on May 4, 2025. [4, 6, 8] The event, which offered various routes including a 75-mile main course through Summerlin and Red Rock Canyon, was organized with the support of the Las Vegas Convention and Visitors Authority and Las Vegas Events. [3, 5] However, the event was canceled on the morning of May 4, 2025, due to unsafe road conditions caused by rain and the forecast of continued lightning, as declared by local public safety officials. [5] This marked the second consecutive year the event was canceled due to weather, with the 2024 edition having been called off because of a severe windstorm. [5, 10] The 1,160 registered cyclists were to be refunded. [5] <10> The return of L'Etape Las Vegas by Tour de France was announced on February 5, 2025, for an event scheduled to take place on Sunday, May 4, 2025. This comes after the 2024 event was canceled due to dangerously high winds. The 2025 amateur cycling event is slated to start and finish near the Las Vegas Ballpark in Summerlin, with multiple course options (75, 45, and 25 miles) that traverse the scenic Red Rock Canyon National Conservation Area on fully closed roads. For the first time, a 14-mile Family Ride will also be offered. Following the 2024 cancellation, registered riders were automatically deferred to the 2025 event. However, conflicting reports from May 4, 2025, stated that the 2025 event was also canceled, this time due to rain and lightning, marking the second consecutive year of weather-related cancellations. According to one report, officials declared the cancellation on the morning of the event due to unsafe road conditions.
